title: htmx 4.0: a Fetch-Based Rewrite, Built-In Morphing Swaps, and Explicit Attribute Inheritance
gist: htmx 4.0 skips version 3 entirely, rewrites the library on fetch() instead of XMLHttpRequest, adds built-in DOM-preserving morphing swaps and explicit attribute inheritance, and ships under npm's next tag so the large existing 2.x user base is never force-upgraded.

insights.claim: htmx 4.0.0 replaces the library's long-standing XMLHttpRequest transport with the modern fetch() API, a rewrite that unlocks native streaming while keeping the script's size around 14KB.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Moving the transport layer to fetch() while holding script size roughly constant shows htmx prioritizing capability gains (streaming) without sacrificing its lightweight-library positioning.
insights.locator: htmx has swapped its long serving XMLHttpRequest transport

insights.claim: htmx creator Carson Gross had publicly promised there would never be an htmx 3, then released version 4.0 after eight months of work, skipping version 3 entirely and summarizing the reversal to InfoWorld with the one-word quote, 'Oops.'
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Skipping a major version number to avoid confusion with an abandoned earlier plan is a small but telling signal of how htmx's small team manages its own roadmap commitments publicly.
insights.locator: Creator Carson Gross, who had promised there would never be an htmx 3

insights.claim: For most developers, the familiar hx-get and hx-post attributes behave exactly as before in htmx 4.0, meaning the underlying transport rewrite is largely invisible at the attribute API level.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Preserving the surface-level API while rewriting internals is a low-risk upgrade strategy that limits breaking changes to a small, identifiable set of features.
insights.locator: For most developers the familiar hx-get and hx-post attributes

insights.claim: htmx 4.0 introduces built-in morphing swaps powered by idiomorph, which preserve DOM state such as input focus during updates, a capability previously requiring a separate extension.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Making morphing a core feature rather than an extension lowers the barrier for developers building interactive server-rendered UIs to get smoother, state-preserving updates by default.
insights.locator: built in morphing swaps powered by idiomorph

insights.claim: A new hx-partial tag in htmx 4.0 lets a single server response cleanly update several page targets at once, offering a tidier alternative to the older out-of-band swap pattern.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Simplifying multi-target updates reduces boilerplate for common server-driven UI patterns, a direct developer-experience improvement.
insights.locator: a new hx-partial tag that lets one response cleanly update several targets

insights.claim: Attribute inheritance in htmx 4.0 is now explicit: parent attributes only reach child elements when the parent attribute is marked with an :inherited suffix, reversing the previous implicit-cascade behavior.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Any app relying on implicit attribute inheritance from htmx 2.x will need an explicit audit before upgrading, since behavior silently changes rather than erroring loudly.

insights.claim: A documented migration trap in htmx 4.0 is that an hx-headers attribute passing a CSRF token to child elements will silently stop working without the new :inherited suffix, causing the server to reject requests with a 403 while nothing in the client appears broken.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A silent security-token failure that manifests only as server-side 403s is exactly the kind of breaking change that can slip past manual testing and needs the official upgrade checker run before deploying.
insights.locator: A detailed DEV Community write up warns this is the trap to watch

insights.claim: htmx 4.0 standardizes event names to an htmx:phase:action pattern, so an event like htmx:afterRequest becomes htmx:after:request, and history no longer snapshots the DOM into localStorage, instead refetching pages so third-party scripts continue to work correctly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Any custom event listeners or third-party integrations tied to the old event names or DOM-snapshot history behavior need updating as part of the 4.0 migration.
insights.locator: Event names have also been standardised to a htmx:phase:action pattern

insights.claim: Beyond the inheritance change, htmx 4.0 adds a new 60-second request timeout and renames several attributes, such as hx-disable becoming hx-ignore, and ships a command-line checker (npx htmx.org@4.0.0 upgrade-check) that flags inheritance issues, renamed attributes, and old events in a codebase.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A dedicated automated upgrade-check tool signals the htmx team anticipated the inheritance and renaming changes would otherwise be too easy to miss manually.
insights.locator: Beyond inheritance changes, there is also a new 60 second request timeout

insights.claim: htmx 4.0 ships under npm's next tag rather than latest, so no one pulling an unversioned CDN link gets force-upgraded, and htmx 2.x remains supported indefinitely.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: This is a deliberately conservative rollout designed to protect the large installed base of production sites on unversioned CDN links from an unannounced breaking change.
insights.locator: htmx 4.0 ships under npm's next tag rather than latest

insights.claim: The htmx team also provides dedicated skills files intended for LLM-assisted upgrades, treating AI coding assistants as a first-class path for migrating existing codebases to 4.0.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Shipping migration tooling explicitly built for AI coding assistants, not just human developers, reflects how library maintainers now expect a meaningful share of upgrade work to be done by AI agents.
insights.locator: dedicated skills files for LLM assisted upgrades

insights.claim: A Hacker News thread on htmx 4.0 passed 700 points, with developers praising the Go, SQLite, and htmx stack and noting that AI coding assistants like Claude handle htmx well, while the r/htmx release post drew over 300 upvotes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Community commentary that an AI assistant 'understands' a framework well is becoming a visible factor in framework adoption and stack recommendations, not just documentation quality or ecosystem size.
insights.quote: understands it and does it well
insights.locator: one noting that Claude "understands it and does it well"

insights.claim: Not all reaction was positive: a .NET and Angular developer argued htmx forces mixing presentation with business logic, and another developer agreed, saying their team is moving back to React.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A live counter-narrative of teams reverting from htmx to React is a reminder that the hypermedia-over-SPA trend is not universally accepted even amid a well-received 4.0 launch.
insights.locator: Elsewhere a .NET and Angular developer argued htmx forces you to mix
